findings.evidence: `rg -n "ContDiffAt\.iteratedDerivWithin_Icc_eq_Ici|iteratedDerivWithin_Icc_eq_Ici" code/TauCeti roadmap` shows the declaration at line 48 and only an implementation use from the private lemma in `CompletelyMonotone/Integral.lean:52-55`; the proof is just `iteratedDerivWithin_eq_iteratedDeriv` on `Icc` and `Ici` at lines 54-56.
findings.fix: Make this lemma private or inline its proof at the private completely-monotone helper unless a concrete roadmap consumer needs the public generic name.
findings.issue: `ContDiffAt.iteratedDerivWithin_Icc_eq_Ici` is still public even though it is only used to prove a private helper, so this exposes a generic two-Mathlib-lemma wrapper as API.

findings.evidence: Current signature at line 101 requires `(hxT : x < T)`, while the underlying Mathlib theorem `intervalIntegral.integral_derivWithin_Icc_of_contDiffOn_Icc` at `mathlib/Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Integral/IntervalIntegral/ContDiff.lean:52` works under `(hab : a ≤ b)`, so downstream users must split off `x = T` themselves.
findings.fix: Generalize the hypothesis to `x ≤ T`, using the existing proof in the strict case and handling `x = T` by simplifying the zero interval.
findings.issue: The public FTC identity `IsCompletelyMonotone.integral_neg_iteratedDerivWithin_one_Ici_eq_sub` requires `x < T`, omitting the degenerate interval case from the characteristic API.

summary: The PR mostly shrinks the surface, but it leaves one generic implementation wrapper public and the new public fixed-half-line FTC lemma is unnecessarily strict, making the characteristic API less usable than the Mathlib theorem it wraps.
